framework.name: ISO/IEC 42005:2025 — AI System Impact Assessment
framework.description: International standard for AI system impact assessment (AISIA). Provides guidance for organisations on how to implement a process for completing AI system impact assessments and promotes a common understanding of the components necessary to produce an effective assessment. Integrates with ISO/IEC 42001 AI management system and ISO/IEC 23894 AI risk management. Two main clauses: Clause 5 (developing and implementing the assessment process) and Clause 6 (documenting the assessment).

objects.title: AI System Impact Assessment Process
objects.description: Developing and implementing the AI system impact assessment process — covers the organisational approach, documentation, integration, timing, scope, responsibilities, thresholds, performance, analysis, recording, approval, and ongoing monitoring of AI system impact assessments.

objects.title: AI System Impact Assessment Documentation
objects.description: Documenting the AI system impact assessment — covers the scope, AI system information, data and algorithm information, deployment environment, relevant interested parties, actual and reasonably foreseeable impacts, and measures to address identified harms and benefits.

objects.title: Assessment Process: General & Documentation
objects.description: Clauses 5.1–5.2. The organisation should have a structured, consistent approach for performing and documenting AI system impact assessments. Documentation should be kept up to date and made available to relevant interested parties.

objects.title: Integration, Timing, Scope & Responsibilities
objects.description: Clauses 5.3–5.6. Integration with other organisational management processes including AI risk management and AI management systems. Determining when assessments should be performed, defining the scope, and allocating responsibilities to appropriate individuals.

objects.title: Thresholds, Performance & Assessment Conduct
objects.description: Clauses 5.7–5.8. Establishing thresholds for sensitive uses, restricted uses, and impact scales. Performing the AI system impact assessment including identification, analysis, and evaluation of impacts.

objects.title: Analysis, Recording, Approval & Monitoring
objects.description: Clauses 5.9–5.12. Analysing the results of the AI system impact assessment. Recording and reporting outcomes. Approval process for AI system impact assessments. Monitoring and review of assessments to ensure continued applicability and effectiveness.

objects.title: Assessment Scope & AI System Information
objects.description: Clauses 6.2–6.3. Documenting the scope of the AI system impact assessment. AI system information including description, functionalities and capabilities, purpose, intended uses, and unintended uses.

objects.title: Data & Algorithm Information
objects.description: Clauses 6.4–6.5. Data information and quality documentation including data sources, quality criteria, and data management. Algorithm and model information including algorithms used, development processes, models deployed, and model development documentation.

objects.title: Deployment Environment & Interested Parties
objects.description: Clauses 6.6–6.7. Deployment environment including geographical area and languages, environment complexity and operational constraints. Relevant interested parties including directly affected parties and other stakeholders.

objects.title: Impact Identification & Mitigation Measures
objects.description: Clauses 6.8–6.9. Actual and reasonably foreseeable impacts including benefits and harms to individuals, groups, and society. AI system failures and reasonably foreseeable misuse scenarios. Measures to address identified harms and realise benefits.
